Economic theory suggests the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my private value of $25. This is because:
1. Bidding less risks losing the item when I would have profited
2. Bidding more risks paying more than the item is worth to me
3. In a single-round game with no repeated interactions, truthful bidding minimizes potential losses
4. The second-price auction mechanism incentivizes honest valuation
So I will bid my exact private value.

Economic theory suggests the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my private value of $31. In a first-price sealed bid auction, bidding less risks losing the item, while bidding more risks negative earnings. Since values are independently and randomly drawn each round, there's no strategic advantage to deviating from a "bid your value" approach. I will bid my full private value to maximize my potential profit.

Economic theory suggests bidding my true value of $9 is the dominant strategy. In a first-price sealed bid auction, bidding below my value risks losing the item, while bidding above risks negative earnings. Since this is a single round with no repeated interactions, the safest strategy is to bid exactly my private value of $9, which maximizes my potential profit if I win.
